guess.note: Fits every equation; still a conjecture beyond the data.

guess_on_first_13_terms.note: Fits every equation; still a conjecture beyond the data.

finite_check.statement: Complete proof if the order bound is itself justified (e.g. by a transfer matrix of that size); otherwise it is evidence.

lesson.structure: transfer: the count is u^T M^n v for an 8x8 integer matrix M (column profiles); local: the leftmost column splits the rectangle into smaller ones: A_m = A_{m-2} + 2 B_{m-1}, B_m = A_{m-1} + B_{m-2}
lesson.recognized: the leftmost column splits the rectangle into smaller ones: A_m = A_{m-2} + 2 B_{m-1}, B_m = A_{m-1} + B_{m-2}
routes_tried: guess: guess a linear recurrence from data, test on held-out terms
polynomial: guess a polynomial formula in n
split: prove it from the column decomposition
lesson.what_failed: polynomial: growth is exponential (ratio -> 2 + sqrt(3)); no polynomial of degree <= 8 fits
lesson.what_worked: split: prove it from the column decomposition. a direct proof, cross-checked by the finite check
lesson.verified_by: compare A_m, B_m with backtracking counts for small boards (the case analysis is exhaustive)
lesson.principle: When a count looks like a linear recurrence, guess it from data, hold terms out, then prove it twice: from a local decomposition and from an order bound plus a finite check.
